rationale: Evidence: iteration 3 (score 361.4) is the best raced design. Its oval finishes reliably at about 1.86 s, but every s-bend and slalom trial goes off track at max_error about 0.062 to 0.063 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit (body_width is already at its maximum). Slalom shows about 1 line-loss event per run with progress stuck near 0.10, which points to the tape leaving the five-sensor span (x = -0.06 to +0.06) at large lateral error. Iteration 5 (sensors at y = 0.08) did not fix the bends, so sensor lead is not the main limit. Iteration 4 (kd 1.0) cost oval finishes and did not fix the bends, so kd stays at 0.8. Iteration 2 changed several things at once and hurt the oval, so its wider span was never tested cleanly. Iteration 1 at base_speed 1.3 and iteration 3 at 1.1 both fail the bends, so speed is not the lever. The untested hypothesis is that the outer sensors lose the tape at large error. This is the one change I make from iteration 3: seven sensors at x = -0.075 to +0.075 in 0.025 m steps (y = 0.06, size 0.012). The 0.025 m spacing keeps at least one 12 mm footprint on a 25 mm tape everywhere in the span. The outer weights rise to +/-1.5, so the steering signal is stronger at large error. Controller gains otherwise match iteration 3 (base 1.1, kp 2.5, ki 0.02, kd 0.8, last_direction). Expected result: line_loss_events on slalom and s-bend fall toward 0, s-bend max_error drops below 0.055 m, and s-bend progress rises above 0.3, with the oval still finishing near 1.9 s. Risks: the larger weights raise the effective gain by about 1.5x, so steering_oscillation may rise above 0.3 on the oval. If that happens, reduce kp to about 2.0 or the outer weights to about 1.2. If line loss disappears but the robot still exits, the limit is turn authority, and the next lever is kp near 3.0 with this wider array. Hypotheses: (a) line loss at large error causes the bend failures; (b) signal scale change needs kp retuning. Measurements wanted: per-track completion, progress, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and completion_time.
